name: B vitamins
short: High vitamin B6 levels, usually from supplements, may cause sensory nerve damage. Folic acid did not change cancer rates over about 5 years in large trials.
text: A systematic review found that high vitamin B6 levels, usually from supplements, may lead to a mainly sensory peripheral neuropathy, with symptoms reported to improve after stopping pyridoxine; the same review found B6 at permitted daily doses has not been proven harmful in people who already have peripheral neuropathy. No safety source on vitamin B12 was found. In a meta-analysis of 13 randomized trials with about 50,000 participants, folic acid supplementation over an average of 5.2 years had no significant effect on overall or site-specific cancer incidence. No interaction data were found in the cited sources.
